Share card plan

A share image for a game: tap Share, get a picture of your progress or completion to post in a story, a chat or a feed. This revisits the share-gamecard branch from April 5 for the site as it is today. Every card below uses your real games, art and numbers, drawn at the actual export size.

How the April branch renders

Left: the April branch, rendered today by its own drawing code, unchanged. Right: the same game in the matching format of the current plan, Detailed type: vertical → portrait 1080×1350 in both Showcase and Trophy; horizontal 1200×400 → landscape 1200×630 (Showcase, the only style with a landscape format).

What's wrong with it
  • Text collides: "100%" overlaps its own label ("100%PLETION"); the HARDCORE chip runs into the @Yozuryu pill
  • Wrong status: Ring of Fates at 1.3% gets a gold HARDCORE badge and a giant "HARDCORE" watermark, read like an award
  • Dead space: the vertical card is half empty at the bottom; the horizontal one crams tiny text into a strip that X and Discord crop
  • Muddy art: the screenshot sits at half opacity behind everything, so neither the art nor the text reads

Why re-implement, not merge

Worth keeping
  • Drawing on a canvas in the browser: no server
  • Two formats, a preview, the native share sheet on phones plus download
  • The content mix: art, icon, title, status, progress, stats, an achievement, your avatar and name
  • Skipping a missing image instead of failing
Why not merge it
  • 7 months behind; the RA page it edits has been rewritten since
  • Share button only on hover: invisible on a phone
  • RA only
  • Every image through a third-party proxy; checked today, RA images and Steam store art can be drawn directly, only Steam achievement icons and Xbox art need it
  • Spinner instead of the site's shimmer skeleton; download via a data-URL link, unreliable in the iOS home-screen app

Proposal

DecisionProposalWhy
Where Share livesA Share button in the achievement modal on all three profiles (tap a game → Share), and on each Completions entryVisible on a phone; every game on every platform; Completions is where the "I finished it" moment is
StylesAll three: Showcase, Trophy and Dashboard, switched in the share sheet; Showcase is the defaultDifferent games suit different styles (Trophy for a completion, Dashboard for a game you're grinding); choosing at share time costs one toggle
FormatsPortrait 1080×1350 (default), Story 1080×1920 (all three styles) and Landscape 1200×630 (Showcase)4:5 is the largest an Instagram feed post shows and reads well in WhatsApp; 9:16 for stories, with text kept out of the top and bottom 250px the app covers; 1200×630 for X and Discord
TypeDetailed or Clean for every style and format: Clean keeps the art, title, progress and identity and drops the rest: no play strip, no rarest achievement, at most two numbersCards are often seen small (landscape in a timeline is ~0.3× size); Clean keeps what is left readable there. Landscape opens on Clean; portrait and story open on Detailed
ArtRA: the game icon over the blurred in-game screenshot (a DS screenshot is cropped to its top screen); no screenshot → the icon over a blur of its own centre, so a dark frame on the icon never shows. RA icons are 96px, drawn at whole-number sizes (2× = 192, 3× = 288) so the pixel art stays crisp. Steam: store hero art; Trophy uses the tall store cover in a progress frame, or the wide header when there is noneSteam's real game icon is 32px, too small to show big
ContentArt · icon · title · platform/console · status · progress · 3 stats · rarest achievement · play strip or road to completion · avatar, name, site · dateCompleted games lead with status and date; in-progress games with progress and recent play
StatsRA: played · points · sessions (or hardcore players when done). Steam: played · sessions · average sessionAll in files the pages already load; nothing new from the pipelines. Steam data has no genre or year
SharingPhone: Share → system share sheet (Instagram, WhatsApp, Save image). Desktop: Download, Copy imageThe share sheet is the reliable way to save an image from the iOS home-screen app
CodeOne shared module, assets/sharecard.js, plus a small modal per pageSame pattern as assets/playing.js

Card styles

Every style comes in two types, shown side by side for each game: Detailed (fuller, with boxes, the strip's axis line and the achievement description) and Clean (art, title, progress, identity and at most two numbers; the strip and the rarest achievement go). Clean exists because cards are often seen small: a landscape image in an X or Discord timeline shows about 360px wide on a phone, roughly 0.3× its size, and 13–15px labels turn into unreadable 4px texture.

Each direction with seven real games (plus one softcore example): RA 7th Dragon 2020 (mastered), Ring of Fates (just started, DS) and Poring Clicker (in progress, no screenshot on RA: the fallback), and Steam STAR OCEAN THE SECOND STORY R (perfect), LEGO City Undercover (beaten, still playing), OCTOPATH TRAVELER and Little Noah (in progress).

Landscape · 1200×630

Showcase reflowed for wide posts (X, Discord), Detailed and Clean side by side, with the same story as the portrait card: progress, stats, the 13-week play strip (or the road to completion) and the rarest achievement. RA: the icon in front of the softly blurred screenshot, at 2× its real size (192px) so the pixel art stays crisp. The art fades out through a mask, so there is no seam in the middle.

Story · 1080×1920

All three styles in 9:16 for Instagram and WhatsApp stories, Detailed and Clean side by side. The app's own UI (profile name at the top, reply bar at the bottom) covers about the top and bottom 250px, marked with dashed lines here (not part of the export): art may run under it, but text, numbers and your identity stay inside the middle.

Build plan

Card renderer (assets/sharecard.js): draw all three styles on a canvas at export size (shared pieces: art, badges, stats, strip, identity), plus the landscape Showcase; RA icons at whole-number scales with smoothing off; blurred backgrounds centred and covering the banner (no black areas); long titles shrink to fit before they're truncated (Ring of Fates in landscape); images direct where CORS allows (RA, Steam store art), proxy only for Steam achievement icons and Xbox art, skipped on failure; wait for fonts before drawing.

Card data per platform: turn each profile's game object into the card's fields (status, progress, stats, rarest achievement, recent badges, play strip), from data the pages already have plus the playtime log.

Share sheet UI: a style switch (Showcase · Trophy · Dashboard), a format switch (portrait · story, plus landscape for Showcase) and a Detailed / Clean switch, the preview (shimmer skeleton while drawing, fades in), Share / Download / Copy; phone-first, following the site's motion rules. The last style picked is remembered.

Entry points: Share in the achievement modal on RA, Steam and Xbox, and on Completions entries.

Check at phone width with real games in every state (mastered, perfect, beaten, in progress, no screenshot, DS, long titles, subsets and hacks), export both formats, compare with the chosen mockup; changelog, docs, push.

Decisions for you

  • Decided: all three styles, switchable when sharing (Showcase default); landscape 1200×630; Trophy on Steam uses the progress frame
  • Decided: story 9:16 ships now, for all three styles
  • Detailed / Clean: keep both as a switch (landscape opening on Clean, recommended), or ship only one
  • Entry points: achievement modal + Completions, or also the Playing tiles
  • Identity: avatar, name and site address on every card, or optional
